text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Front page editorial says the Democratic Party strongly supports the March 9 agreement of the ten political parties and calls on the Socialist Party to do the same thing.
- Tritan Shehu, leader of the Democratic Party, thanks the Italian people, government and parliament for sending their troops in Albania to support the humanitarian aid distribution.
- The Democratic Party and Socialist Party MPs agree to relax the censorship measures for the press.
- Still chaos in the southern towns of Gramsh and Sarande. A policeman was killed in the northern town of Shkoder. A four-year old child died after a bomb explosion.
- Despite more attacks against President Sali Berisha, supported by a group of the Democratic Party MPs, he has still not completed his historical mission, a commentary said.

- The Italian parliament approves sending troops in Albania. The Albanian crisis alarms (Italian PM Romano) Prodi but not (Albanian President Sali) Berisha!...While Prodi follows with concern in Rome the parliamentary debate for troops coming to Albania, Berisha in Tirana mulls how he may justify his re-election.
- Socialist leaders hold meetings with their branches in different districts of the country.
- Berisha and his supporters at the Democratic Party are not interested in holding the elections in June.

- After a suspension of one month the newspaper resumed publication, the paper in editorial says this is a sign which shows the situation is going towards normalcy in Tirana, but laments fact that the press did not cover one of the most difficult periods in the country's history.
- The Interior Ministry says more than 200 died and about 700 were injured during the recent unrest in the country.
- Two prisons in Tirana are ready to function again while ten courts buildings in the country have been destroyed.
- Public order in southeastern town of Korce going towards normalcy after the itnervention of some special police troops.
- Albania's exiled king Leka I will return to Albania on Saturday.
- The first round of Albanian-Serbian talks in New York, sponsored by a U.S. non-governmental foundation, was over.
